Dobro起源於1920年代，John Dopyera與George Beauc: Dobro began in the 1920s, when John Dopyera and George Beauchamp developed resonator guitars to get more volume; in 1929 Dopyera left National and founded Dobro with his brothers. Its single-cone, outward-facing design supports the bridge on an eight-legged aluminium spider and is louder and cheaper than the three-cone type. In 1932 the Dopyera brothers merged National and Dobro; after the 1940s the brand changed hands several times, passed to Gibson in 1993 and was later made by Epiphone. It entered country music from 1939.

演奏多布羅吉他時，可依其結構理解發聲順序：琴弦振動經琴橋傳至八腳鋁製蜘蛛，蜘蛛位: When playing a Dobro, follow its structure to understand the order of sound: the strings' vibration passes through the bridge to the eight-legged aluminium spider, which sits at the rim of the single cone, and that drives the outward-facing concave cone. A beginner should note that this differs from the three-cone design: the point is the single outward cone and the spider's transmission, not the vibration of a flat wooden soundboard as on an ordinary acoustic guitar.
